title: Vendor-published endpoint files can name most of what the NDH cannot
headline: Vendors already publish the organization behind 61,161 of the 95,012 NDH FHIR endpoints that carry no owner (64%). 29,566 of those resolve to an NPI directly. Ingesting files that are public today would move endpoint attribution from 14.6% to 69.6%.
notes:
The gap measured in H50 is not absent data. It is data published by the EHR vendors and not carried into the directory. PointClickCare publishes 4,015 endpoints and the NDH holds exactly 4,015 of them at zero attribution, so the name was available at ingest time.

Two publication styles. Most vendors ship a flat HTI-1 service base URL list, one endpoint per practice. Epic ships a SMART User-access Brands bundle, where care sites hang off a parent brand and the endpoint sits on the brand. The hierarchy is the more useful shape: naming one endpoint names every care site beneath it.

Reference resolution decides whether this works at all. Epic references bundle entries by urn:uuid rather than Type/id and links care sites by partOf. A naive resolver returns zero matches, which is the same failure that produced a wrong published claim about Epic in H47. Both reference styles and both link directions are handled, and the hierarchy rollup is asserted against the organization count so a double-count cannot pass silently.

The crosswalk CSV has one row per (url, org_npi); a URL with no NPI has one row with an empty org_npi. Since FHI-73 a URL may repeat, once per NPI its publisher lists: 74,243 url-NPI pairs (published_url_npi_pairs) across 70,378 URLs. Earlier files kept only the first NPI per URL. The last column, npis_on_url, is the number of distinct NPIs the vendor lists for that URL (0 on a row with no NPI). 37,909 of the 74,243 pairs (51.1%) sit on a URL listing more than 10 NPIs (npis_on_url_bands). Those are practice-wide or brand-wide lists: athenahealth attaches the same practice list to every department entry, and Epic brands list up to hundreds. The NPI is genuinely published beside the URL, but it does not say which organization the URL serves, so the connectivity ledger counts such a match as its own tier (vendor-npi-list), not as deterministic. org_name is the first vendor entry listing the NPI; for practice-wide lists it may name a sibling department (20,433 url-NPI pairs are listed by more than one differently named entry). Vendor-wide shared base URLs, which every customer of the vendor uses and which identify no organization, are excluded entirely (https://api.platform.athenahealth.com/fhir/r4; 125,911 organization references dropped).

Every figure is a floor. These are the largest publishers; ONC's Lantern catalogues over 200 sources. Matching is exact on a normalized URL, so a vendor that spells a path differently from the NDH is counted as a miss.

The vendor files carry visible test data. Practice Fusion publishes an organization named 'Practice Fusion Test Test account' and an address line reading 'Helloooo This is important'. Anything built on these needs a junk filter, or it republishes that as fact.
